examples.name: Checked
examples.description: A checkbox can be initially checked using `defaultChecked`, or controlled via the `checked` property.

examples.name: Mixed
examples.description:
A checkbox can be initially mixed (also known as indeterminate) using `defaultChecked="mixed"`, or controlled via `checked="mixed"`.
In this example, the mixed state is used when a group of options has differing values.

examples.name: Large
examples.description: A checkbox can be large in size.

examples.name: Label Before
examples.description: The label can be placed before the checkbox.

examples.name: Label Wrapping
examples.description: The label will wrap if it is wider than the available space. The checkbox indicator will stay aligned to the first line of text.

examples.name: Required
examples.description: When a checkbox is marked as `required`, its label also gets the required styling.

examples.name: Circular
examples.description:
A checkbox can have a circular shape.
**Usage warning**: Unless you are designing a tasks experience, we strongly discourage using this styling variant, as it can be confused with `RadioItem`.
